newsitem.title: USA: National Park Service director to resign.
newsitem.headline: National Park Service director to resign.

text.p: The director of the National Park Service plans to resign as soon as his replacement is ready to take up the post, the Interior Department said Monday.

Roger Kennedy, appointed by President Clinton in 1993, said in a statement he had planned to retire after four years in the job overseeing 374 parks in 49 states, the District of Columbia and five territories.
Under the Omnibus Parks and Public Lands Management Act that was passed last year, the new parks director, for the first time, will have to be confirmed by the Senate.
That process could take several weeks or months once Clinton nominates a replacement, and Kennedy's resignation would take effect upon his replacement's confirmation.
